mainEntity.name: How long does it take to design and erect a pre-engineered metal building?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical pre-engineered metal building project takes anywhere from a few months to over half a year from initial planning to completion. The process starts with structural design and engineering calculations, followed by local permitting. Once plans are approved, off-site steel fabrication generally takes several weeks. While components are manufactured, on-site grading, excavation, and concrete slab work take place. When the steel package arrives on-site, erection moves quickly, often taking one to three weeks depending on the structure's square footage and roof height. Mechanical rough-ins and interior finishing follow afterward.
acceptedAnswer.description: The entire process usually takes several months, including engineering, permitting, off-site manufacturing, foundation pouring, and one to three weeks for steel erection.
